title: Normalized terminal sections and derived scalar change at a normed point
statement:
Work in compatible small-site and coefficient universes. Let $F$ be a normed field with totally disconnected metric topology, put $C_F(P)=C(P,F)$ for profinite $P$ [def-sfb-continuous-map-condensed-ring], and put $F_T=p_T^*C_F$ for every scheme $T$ [sk-def-sfb-pulled-back-coefficients]. Modules mean internal $F_T$-modules [sk-def-sfb-module-objects], with module inverse images as in [sk-def-sfb-module-pushforward-pullback]. Let $k$ be algebraically closed and put $s=\operatorname{Spec}k$. Let $F\hookrightarrow F'$ be a continuous field inclusion into another totally disconnected normed field, inducing $F_s\to F'_s$ by postcomposition on continuous functions [def-sfb-continuous-map-condensed-ring-map]. Write $E_F(N)=\Gamma(s,N)$ as an abstract $F$-vector space using the constant-section identification $\Gamma(s,F_s)=F$, and similarly define $E_{F'}$. Restriction $\operatorname{Res}_{F'_s/F_s}$ is exact [def-sfb-modobj-restriction], and there is a natural identification
$$E_F(\operatorname{Res}_{F'_s/F_s}N)=\operatorname{Res}_{F'/F}E_{F'}(N)$$
with identity underlying additive map. The ordinary balanced maps give natural isomorphisms
$$F'\otimes_F E_F(M)\xrightarrow{\sim}E_{F'}(F'_s\otimes_{F_s}M),\qquad a\otimes m\longmapsto a\otimes m,$$
for the relative sheaf tensor [def-sfb-modobj-relative-tensor, def-pur-sheaf-tensor-product]. All these identifications respect $m\mapsto1\otimes m$. Write $E_F^D,E_{F'}^D$ for the exact termwise sections functors on ordinary unbounded derived categories [sk-def-sfb-derived-categories]. For every $K\in D(\operatorname{Mod}_{F_s})$ there is a natural isomorphism in $D(\operatorname{Vect}_{F'})$
$$F'\otimes_F^{\mathbf L}E_F^D(K)\xrightarrow{\sim}E_{F'}^D(F'_s\otimes_{F_s}^{\mathbf L}K).$$
On every K-flat resolution $P\to K$ [def-pc-kflat-complex] this isomorphism is represented by the displayed degreewise balanced map. It commutes with replacement maps and differentials and takes the scalar-adjunction insertion-of-one unit to the insertion-of-one unit. Restriction also commutes with termwise sections on these derived categories. There is no boundedness, constructibility, completeness, or flatness hypothesis on $F_s\to F'_s$.

proof.text: Put $R=F_s$, $S=F'_s$, $a:R\to S$, $E=E_F$ and $E'=E_{F'}$. By [lem-sfb-normed-point-exact-monoidal], applied with $Z=s$ and $x=\mathrm{id}_s$, both section functors are exact and their constant-section coefficient maps are isomorphisms. Postcomposition with the continuous inclusion sends a constant function with value $r$ to the constant function with value its image in $F'$ [def-sfb-continuous-map-condensed-ring-map]. Thus the induced section-ring map is the given $F\to F'$. The sheaf tensor with any object preserves colimits by closedness [sk-def-sfb-sheaf-tensor]. Hence [lem-sfb-modobj-restriction-finite-exact] applies to $a$ and makes internal scalar restriction exact. By its definition [def-sfb-modobj-restriction], restriction leaves every section and every additive map unchanged; its action is $r n=a(r)n$. Evaluating this action proves $E\operatorname{Res}_a=\operatorname{Res}_{F'/F}E'$ with identity underlying additive map.

source.place: Example 3.1 and Section 3, printed p.6; Lemma 4.1(1), printed p.8. Internal restriction exactness expanded using the finite universal-property lemma.

proof.text:
Let $N=\operatorname{Res}_a S$. By [lem-sfb-restricted-extension-relative-tensor], restriction of ordinary extension is canonically $N\otimes_R M$, with the comparison fixed by the same coequalizer projection. The tensorator of [lem-sfb-normed-point-exact-monoidal], applied to $N,M$, therefore gives
$$F'\otimes_F E(M)=E(N)\otimes_F E(M)\xrightarrow{\sim}E'(S\otimes_R M).$$
The underlying formula is $b_M(t\otimes m)=[t\otimes m]$. This is $F'$-linear: for $u,t\in F'$, both the image of $(ut)\otimes m$ and multiplication by $u$ after the map are $[(ut)\otimes m]$. The balancing relation is $[ta(r)\otimes m]=[t\otimes rm]$. Naturality follows by applying a module map to $m$ on either path. On $1\otimes m$ the result is $[1\otimes m]$, proving the ordinary insertion-of-one normalization. These checks use the specified generators, not arbitrary choices of isomorphisms.

source.place: Section 3 coefficient adjunction and Lemma 4.1(1), ordinary balanced calculation at the terminal point.

proof.text: Write $t(V)=F'\otimes_F V$. The $F$-module $F'$ is flat by [lem-weil-pbc-module-over-field-flat]; [lem-weil-pbc-flat-tensor-exact] shows that $t$ is exact. Consequently [lem-weil-pbc-exact-functor-derived-factorization] gives exact termwise functors $D(t),E^D,E'^D,D(\operatorname{Res}_a)$ and the ordinary field restriction, all preserving quasi-isomorphisms. Field restriction and its exactness can also be read on the singleton site via [lem-weil-pbc-singleton-site-module-comparison] and [lem-pur-sheaf-ring-coefficient-ordinary-adjunction]. The identity section comparison of step 1 is an identity in every complex degree; its localization is the derived restriction/sections comparison, by [lem-weil-pbc-localization-universal-property]. The same property identifies composites of these exact termwise functors with the termwise composite, retaining the identity underlying maps.

source.place: Ordinary unbounded interpretation of Section 3; Stacks derived.tex Tag 015F; sites-modules.tex Tags 03DA, 03D7; categories.tex Tag 04VG.

proof.text:
Use the exact internal/sectionwise scalar comparison [lem-sfb-internal-section-scalar-adjunction] to work with the reconstructed ring sheaves $R,S$. By [lem-pe-internal-section-tensor-comparison], this operation preserves all K-flat complexes and total tensors, with the same pure tensors. The K-flat scalar extension $T=S\otimes_R^{\mathbf L}-$ has, on every K-flat complex $P$, the canonical natural isomorphism
$$c_P:T(QP)\xrightarrow{\sim}Q(S\otimes_R P)$$
by [lem-pur-derived-change-of-rings]; exchanging the scalar factor to the first position sends $p\otimes t$ to $t\otimes p$. Resolutions with flat terms exist for every unbounded complex by [lem-pc-kflat-resolution]. On the singleton site [lem-weil-pbc-singleton-site-module-comparison], the same derived-change-of-rings theorem computes $F'\otimes_F^{\mathbf L}-$; since $t$ is exact, its comparison with $D(t)$ is canonical by [def-sfb-left-derived-exact]. Thus $D(t)$ computes the left-hand scalar tensor even when the evaluated complex has not been shown K-flat.

source.place: Section 3; Stacks sites-cohomology.tex Tags 06YS, 06YT, 06YU, 06YY; exact-functor comparison dual to derived.tex Tag 015F.

proof.text:
On the homotopy category of $R$-complexes put $A(P)=D(t)E^D(QP)$ and $B(P)=E'^D T(QP)$. Both functors invert every quasi-isomorphism, since they factor through $Q$. For K-flat $P$ define
$$\alpha_P=(E'^D(c_P))^{-1}\circ Q(b_P):A(P)\xrightarrow{\sim}B(P),$$
with the canonical exact-section factorizations understood. Here $b_P$ has component $b_{P^n}$ in degree $n$; it is a chain isomorphism, because both composites with the differential send $t\otimes p$ to $[t\otimes d_Pp]$. Naturality of the scalar counit and of $b$ proves naturality of $\alpha$ on all maps between K-flat complexes. Apply [lem-sc-nattrans-from-resolving-class] to the full class of K-flat complexes: the required right calculus is [lem-pc-quasi-isomorphisms-multiplicative-system], and existence of resolving maps is [lem-pc-kflat-resolution] together with the internal comparison in step 4. This gives $\beta:A\to B$ on the homotopy category. For a resolution $v:P\to C$, naturality says $B(v)\alpha_P=\beta_C A(v)$. All three other maps are invertible, so $\beta_C=B(v)\alpha_P A(v)^{-1}$ is invertible. By [lem-weil-pbc-localization-universal-property], $\beta$ descends to a natural isomorphism on the entire derived category. This is the required comparison after step 4's identification $D(t)=F'\otimes_F^{\mathbf L}-$; in particular its naturality includes every derived morphism.

source.place: Agent resolving-class expansion of Section 3 and Lemma 4.1(1); Stacks derived.tex Tag 05RT and sites-cohomology.tex Tags 06YS, 06YT, 06YY.

proof.text:
For any K-flat resolution $P\to C$, the comparison of step 5 restricts to $\alpha_P$, and $c_P$ is the K-flat computation map [lem-pur-derived-change-of-rings]. Thus it is represented by precisely the degreewise balanced $b_P$, also when the terms of $P$ are not flat. The formula $b_{P^{n+1}}(t\otimes d_Pp)=d[b_{P^n}(t\otimes p)]$ proves differential compatibility; the scalar has degree zero so there is no additional sign. For a replacement map $u:P\to P'$ the equation is
$$E'^D(c_{P'})\beta_{QP'}D(t)E^D(Qu)=Q(b_{P'})D(t)E^D(Qu)=Q(S\otimes_Ru)Q(b_P).$$
Naturality of $c$ and $b$ proves this equality. Inverting a replacement quasi-isomorphism gives the same equality for its inverse. For any roof $C\xleftarrow{v}H\xrightarrow{f}J$, naturality of the descended comparison gives $B(f)B(v)^{-1}\beta_C=\beta_J A(f)A(v)^{-1}$. This also proves independence of all resolutions; the full faithfulness assertion of [lem-weil-pbc-localization-universal-property] makes the transformation uniquely determined by its resolving components.

source.place: Stacks sites-cohomology.tex Tags 06YT, 06YU, 06YY, canonical resolution comparison; categories.tex Tag 04VG, localization of transformations.

proof.text: Choose a flat-term K-flat resolution $P\to C$. By [lem-pur-sheaf-ring-derived-coefficient-adjunction], the scalar-adjunction unit on $QP$ is represented by $p\mapsto p\otimes1$, or $p\mapsto1\otimes p$ with our factor order. The internal comparison [lem-sfb-internal-section-scalar-adjunction] preserves this adjunction and its unit. On the field side the identical assertion follows by applying the same derived-adjunction theorem to the singleton site [lem-weil-pbc-singleton-site-module-comparison]. By step 2, $b_P$ carries $1\otimes p$ to $[1\otimes p]$ in each degree. Under the restriction identity of step 3, this proves the unit square on $QP$. Naturality transports the equality across the resolution isomorphism $QP\cong QC$, and every derived object has such a representative. Hence the square holds everywhere. The comparison therefore preserves the specified insertion-of-one units and the derived restriction comparison. All resolutions and localizations used are unbounded; no exactness of $S\otimes_R-$ or flatness of $R\to S$ has been assumed.
